name: motor-driver-pours
prompt: Two amp buck feeding a motor driver, TPS62933, two ounce outer copper, JLCPCB. There are four M3 mounting holes and the heatsink bolts through two of them. I need the power path to carry the current and the pour not to break up around the holes.

inputs.substrate: a JLCPCB stackup with two ounce outer copper
inputs.notes: Heavy copper changes what the fab will make, so a width taken from a one ounce table is the wrong number. M3 clearance holes are non-plated and copper must keep away from them. A pour threading between four holes is where minimum feature size and sliver removal stop being theoretical.
inputs.environment: Commands run from the repository root with an interpreter that has jitx installed and a reachable runtime.

expected_output: A rule set whose conductor widths are justified for two ounce copper at the stated current, with copper-to-hole clearance, a minimum pour feature size, and a thermal pad treatment, plus checks on the captured design.

assertions.text: the power conductor width is justified for the stated current on two ounce copper, and a one ounce figure is not carried over without adjustment
copper-to-hole clearance is declared against the non-plated mounting holes, and the heatsink holes are not treated as ordinary clearance holes without saying why
a minimum pour feature size is set and the realized pour is checked for slivers and orphaned islands rather than assumed intact
the thermal pad is either direct connect or relief, declared deliberately, and the choice is measured on the captured design rather than trusted
every declared rule is witnessed, and clearance_relaxations reports no relaxation or names how one was resolved
no check passes on an empty selection
the checker library the skill routes to is importable
